routine.name: love-tap improvement loop
routine.delivery: self-bound: the Routine wakes the session that created it, and that session spawns a fresh repository-attached worker per firing with create_session
designs_that_do_not_work: Routine mints a fresh session which pushes: a minted session gets sources: [] and the proxy injects no push credential, so git push is a deterministic 403.

The minted session attaches the repository itself: it has no MCP tools. One probe told to call add_repo then push landed nothing; another told to call create_session produced no session and returned in eight seconds.

Routine wakes a named persistent orchestrator: its container had been reclaimed and the wake never re-provisioned it. Fired 22:20; the session's updated_at never moved and the Routine recorded no last_run at all.
traps_paid_for_already: list_triggers reports last_run SUCCEEDED for a firing that achieved nothing: it records delivery, not accomplishment. A commit on origin is the only proof.

update_trigger has no persistent_session_id parameter -- only create_trigger does. Passing it to update_trigger is silently ignored, so a rebinding needs the Routine recreated. Read persist_session back rather than trusting the call.
create_session cannot make a child more permissive than its parent, so a dispatcher must be created from a session that is not in plan mode or it inherits plan and stalls for ever.
routine.when_it_stops: The dispatcher is a real session with a real context window. If it fills or is archived the loop stops silently and the branch simply stops gaining commits. The fix is to create the Routine again from a new session, which is two calls; nothing is lost because loop/STATE.json holds the state.
